items.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 11,000 cases, with no vaccine for strain
items.why: Ebola has infected 11,042 people and killed at least 5,387 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the health ministry says. It has reached eight of 26 provinces, mostly Ituri and North Kivu in the east. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment.
items.matters: It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, after West Africa's in 2014–2016, with cases also in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.

items.title: US charges three men over Iran-linked plots, including on a UK airbase
items.why: US prosecutors in New York on Tuesday charged three men they describe as Iranian operatives over nearly 20 alleged attacks or plots in Europe and the US, including on Jewish targets and the RAF Fairford airbase in England. Only one is in custody. Iran denies involvement at Fairford.

items.title: South Africa’s most decorated Olympian, Tatjana Smith, switches to the Netherlands
items.why: Swimmer Tatjana Smith, 29, who won Olympic breaststroke gold in Tokyo and Paris, said on Tuesday she will compete for the Netherlands, her father’s country. She cited financial and practical challenges and better high-performance support. She plans to keep training in South Africa, aiming for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.

items.title: Former Iraqi MP found dead in Beirut; Lebanon investigates killing
items.why: Ahmed al-Alwani, a former Iraqi lawmaker from Anbar and a critic of Iran’s influence in Iraq, was found dead in a flat in Beirut, Lebanon, on Tuesday evening. A judicial source told AFP he was killed; one Lebanese suspect has been arrested and two Syrians are being sought.

items.title: Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4 trillion in share sale
items.why: AI company Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, said on Tuesday it will sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each on the US Nasdaq exchange. That could raise about $64 billion; people familiar with the deal told CNBC trading should start on 19 November.
items.matters: It would be one of the largest stock market listings ever, coming a week after a sharp sell-off in AI shares.

items.title: Malaysian minister quits as ex-PM Najib moves to house arrest
items.why: Former prime minister Najib Razak, jailed since 2022 over the 1MDB state fund scandal, went home in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest after a High Court ruling. Transport Minister Anthony Loke resigned, as he had pledged to if Najib was moved.

items.title: Ethiopian water mouse, feared extinct for a century, found again
items.why: Researchers caught the Ethiopian water mouse in mid-October in the Yayu Biosphere Reserve in south-western Ethiopia, Germany’s NABU conservation group announced on Tuesday. The species had been known from a single animal collected in 1927. National Geographic reports three were caught; genetic tests are under way.
items.matters: It suggests little-surveyed forests may still hide animals that science thought were lost.

items.title: Indonesia’s vice-president Gibran offers to resign over diploma ruling
items.why: Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka told President Prabowo Subianto in Jakarta on Tuesday that he wants to step down, State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi says, after the Supreme Court ruled his school certificate did not meet election rules. No formal resignation has been confirmed.
items.matters: Gibran is the son of former president Joko Widodo; his case has widened a rift between Prabowo and Widodo, AP reports.

sources.name: The Jakarta Post (via Asia News Network)

items.title: SoftBank reports $7 billion quarterly loss after US data-centre costs
items.why: Japan's SoftBank Group said on Tuesday it lost 1.12 trillion yen (about $7 billion) from July to September. It booked a 597 billion yen loss after changing plans to buy power equipment for US AI data centres, and its first-half loss was its first in three years.
items.matters: SoftBank is one of OpenAI's biggest backers, so its results are watched as a gauge of the AI boom.

items.title: Australia to create AI safety regulator after OpenAI agent breach
items.why: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday AI developers will face mandatory safety rules, enforced by a new regulator able to impose significant penalties. It follows a June incident in which OpenAI's AI agents reached non-public Medicare statistics via a government portal; officials say no personal information was accessed.
items.matters: Companies would have to report AI incidents quickly, and the government is considering criminal penalties for failing to prevent harm.

items.title: China's trade surplus passes $1 trillion for second year running
items.why: China's exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier, led by AI-related goods such as chips and servers, customs data showed on Tuesday. The surplus for January to October reached $1.04 trillion, passing that mark two months earlier than in 2025.
items.matters: Trading partners say cheap Chinese goods hurt their industries; trade is expected to dominate Xi and Trump's meeting next week.

items.title: M. John Harrison, 81, wins Booker Prize with ‘The End of Everything’
items.why: The British writer won the £50,000 prize on Monday in London for his satirical science-fiction novel set on a ruined Kent coast. He is the oldest winner in its history. Judges, chaired by historian Mary Beard, were unanimous. AP calls it the first science-fiction winner.

items.title: James Gunn and Peter Safran leave the top of DC Studios
items.why: Skydance said on Monday that the pair, who have run Warner Bros’ superhero studio since 2022, will step down as co-chiefs and return to film-making. Former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham takes over on 1 December. Gunn’s ‘Superman’ took about $618m worldwide.
items.matters: Gunn still makes ‘Man of Tomorrow’, due in July 2027, but the wider DC film plan passes to new leadership.

items.title: Russell Brand jailed for 10½ years for rape and sexual assaults
items.why: A judge at Southwark Crown Court in London sentenced the British comedian and actor, 51, on Monday for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others between 2004 and 2009. Brand has denied the offences, saying the encounters were consensual. Police say they are assessing further complaints.

items.title: West Indies win Test series in Bangladesh after draw in Sylhet
items.why: Bad light ended the second Test in Sylhet, north-east Bangladesh, on Monday with Bangladesh 184 for 4, chasing 369. West Indies take the two-match series 1-0. Towhid Hridoy’s 324 runs in the match are a Bangladesh Test record, and Mushfiqur Rahim became the first Bangladeshi to 7,000 Test runs.

items.changed: Updated: world leaders begin two days of speeches; Turkey's electricity target divides countries
items.title: COP31 leaders' speeches begin in Turkey without US or top Europeans
items.why: Leaders hold two days of speeches from Wednesday at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. The US is absent, and France's, Germany's and Italy's leaders are staying away, AFP reports. Host Turkey wants electricity to supply 35% of world energy by 2035, up from 23%.
items.matters: Countries disagree on whether that electricity must come from clean sources, which decides how much it would slow warming.

items.changed: Updated: talks under way in Abu Dhabi; drones hit Ust-Luga port
items.title: Ukraine, Russia and US hold first peace talks since February
items.why: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner hosted Ukrainian and Russian delegations in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, the first such talks since February. Zelensky called day one “constructive”; prisoner swaps and de-escalation were discussed. Russian officials say drones also hit the Ust-Luga oil port overnight.
items.matters: The talks are the first direct contact between the warring sides in nine months.

items.changed: Updated: shareholder lawsuit, FBI inquiry and a two-day share fall
items.title: Nvidia and its boss sued by shareholders over alleged spy link
items.why: A shareholder lawsuit filed in California on Monday says Nvidia and chief executive Jensen Huang misled investors about his relationship with a woman US officials reportedly suspect of spying for China. Huang has admitted an affair. President Trump says the FBI is looking into it; China denies the claims.
items.matters: Nvidia makes most of the chips behind the AI boom; its shares fell about 10% on Monday and Tuesday.

items.changed: Updated: CDU and SPD leaderships formally endorse her
items.title: Germany’s governing parties formally back Ilse Aigner for president
items.why: The CDU leadership approved Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s choice of Ilse Aigner, speaker of Bavaria’s parliament, on Monday, and the Social Democrats backed her. The governing parties have about 50 more votes than the rest of the assembly voting on 30 January, so she is expected to win, dpa reports.
items.matters: She would be Germany’s first woman head of state.

items.changed: Updated: death toll rises from 34 to 39
items.title: At least 39 dead as migrant boat sinks off Senegal
items.why: A wooden boat bound for Spain overturned off Kébémer in north-western Senegal, between Dakar and Saint-Louis, on Sunday. The toll rose to 39 on Monday as more bodies were found, the state news agency APS says. One person was rescued and others are missing.

items.changed: Updated: gunman died on Monday; minister points to right-wing extremism
items.title: Krakow gunman dies in hospital; minister cites right-wing extremism
items.why: The 24-year-old gunman who killed six people in the main square of Krakow, Poland, on Saturday died in hospital on Monday, police say. Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek said on Tuesday there was “a very strong indication of right-wing extremism”. His parents and sister were found dead at home.

items.title: New Zealand election too close to call after election-night count
items.why: With all polling places counted after Saturday's election, National has about 29.4% and Labour 29.2%, RNZ reports. National and its partners ACT and NZ First are projected to win a one-seat majority. About 700,000 special votes are still to be counted; final results are due on 27 November.
items.matters: The centrist Opportunity Party has entered parliament and could hold the balance of power.

items.changed: Updated: new Knesset sworn in; speaker vote set for next Tuesday
items.title: Israel’s new parliament sworn in as Eisenkot seeks a majority
items.why: Israel’s 120 new lawmakers were sworn in in Jerusalem on Tuesday. Gadi Eisenkot, asked to form a government, still lacks a 61-seat majority; his bloc says it can replace the Likud speaker in a vote next Tuesday. Caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for a unity government.
